title: Coalescer stall leading to long-tail latency and unequal queueing
creator: Aisha Patel
incident_summary: On 2026-02-18 we observed repeated spikes in 95/99th token latency for hosted text-generation routes. Investigation showed a recurring stall in the batch coalescer that prevented new requests from being aggregated for 80-400ms windows, causing a small subset of requests to experience long-tail latencies and creating unfair queueing across tenants.
timeline: 2026-02-18 03:12 UTC: Pager alert - 95th latency on /v1/generate exceeded 600ms for three minutes (multi-region).
2026-02-18 03:15 UTC: Ops routed traffic to fallback model variants; latency dropped for bulk traffic but isolated long tails persisted.
2026-02-18 03:30 UTC: Initial hypothesis - bursty traffic overload; started increasing batch window heuristics on affected nodes as emergency mitigation.
2026-02-18 05:00 UTC: Rollback of a recent scheduler tweak (PR#4219) to test correlation; long-tail events reduced but not eliminated.
2026-02-19 09:00 UTC: Root cause analysis session convened with runtime, infra, and SRE teams.
2026-02-24 14:00 UTC: Reproduced a coalescer stall in lab with controlled seq-length skew and priority inversion tests.
2026-03-01 11:00 UTC: Canary of fix (PR#4338) deployed to limited fleets; observed 60% reduction in 99th latency on canary.
2026-03-08 16:00 UTC: Runbook updated and owners assigned for ongoing monitoring and automation of the mitigation.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC: This ticket opened to track remaining action items and harden permanent fix for release runtime-1.22.
root_cause: A recently merged optimization to reduce scheduling overhead introduced a corner case where the coalescer's wake-up timer could be repeatedly deferred when sequences with atypical tokenization distributions arrived concurrently with high-priority streaming requests. The deferred wake-ups allowed the coalescer to skip forming batches for short windows (80-400ms) while backlog metrics did not spike enough to trigger emergency fallback, producing uneven queuing and long-tail latency for the affected subset.
mitigation_and_workarounds: Short-term: increased minimum wake frequency for the coalescer in the managed fleets (applied 2026-02-18).
Medium-term: rolled back parts of PR#4219 that suppressed wake events under low backlog pressure (rolled 2026-02-18).
Emergency: automated fallback to smaller fixed-size batches when coalescer inactivity exceeds 150ms (canaryed 2026-03-01).
Runbook: Added a dedicated alert for coalescer-inactivity-duration and an automated remediation playbook to trigger adaptive batch windows and notify owners.
action_items: ENG-31147-A1: Implement deterministic unit+integration tests that simulate tokenization skew + priority inversion to catch coalescer deferral regressions (owner: Miguel Hernandez, estimate: 3).
ENG-31147-A2: Add a telemetry metric 'coalescer_inactivity_ms' and expose 95/99 percentiles per region and model in Console (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-20).
ENG-31147-A3: Rework wake/timer logic to guarantee a hard upper bound on inactivity (max 100ms) even under prioritized traffic; include a formal proof sketch in PR (owner: Runtime team, estimate: 5).
ENG-31147-A4: Update rollout policy to require coalescer telemetry check as a gate for scheduling-related PRs; add to CI smoke tests (owner: Developer Experience, estimate: 2).
ENG-31147-A5: Post-deploy evaluation: 72h latency analysis and fairness report after runtime-1.22 rollout; assign to Performance Eng (owner: Priya Singh, estimate: 2).
ENG-31147-A6: Customer communication: draft templated incident header for affected customers with mitigation summary and expected timelines (owner: CS Ops, due: 2026-03-15).
current_progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Reproduction harness updated to run tokenization skew scenarios automatically in CI (partial).
2026-03-01: Canary deployment of automated small-batch fallback (PR#4338) reduced 99th latency by ~60% on canary fleet (observed over 48h).
2026-03-05: Telemetry schema for 'coalescer_inactivity_ms' approved; SRE started ingestion pipeline work.
2026-03-10: Runtime team drafted a patch reworking timer semantics; internal design review scheduled for 2026-03-14.
2026-03-12: Added action items to require coalescer telemetry gate in scheduling PR checklist; awaiting DX PR to add CI hooks.
risks_and_open_questions: Will a strict max inactivity bound increase overall average latency due to more frequent smaller batches? Needs cost/latency simulation.
Edge cases where aggressive fallback to fixed-size batches may harm throughput for very large models - we need model-profiled thresholds.
Interplay with KV-cache reuse: ensuring smaller batches do not substantially increase cache misses or evictions under peak load.
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-03-01: Canary fallback to smaller fixed batches is acceptable as a stopgap because it has minimal code surface and immediate benefits.
Decision 2026-03-10: Permanent fix will prioritize a hard inactivity ceiling plus an adaptive backoff that increases batch window only when safe (to preserve amortized throughput).
Design trade-off: prefer deterministic timers over opportunistic suppression to avoid nondeterministic latency spikes in multi-tenant scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: coalescer_inactivity_ms' 99th percentile < 100ms across canary fleets for 72h
No regression in median token latency (>2%) after applying hard inactivity bound in performance CI
Console shows per-route fairness metrics and alerts firing for coalescer inactivity within 7 days of rollout
All action items completed or transitioned into separate tickets with owners assigned before release branch cut.
